# Deck collation counting and packing automation

# Deck collation counting and packing automation — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Deck collation counting and packing automation. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] The Morgana Countron AT Touch page uses different mechanism labels: its descriptive paragraph says twin-blade counting, while its specification field says Pin & blade. Preserve both descriptions pending model-specific clarification. (low confidence) — https://plockmaticgroup.com/morgana/product/countron-touch-at/
- [statement] Uchida describes EZC-250 batch counting and interval timing as helping an operator collect a designated number of items; it also describes automatic retry after a slipped feed. Treat operator collection as a labor step when evaluating this counter. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=287

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Duplo lists a DSC-10/60i input minimum of 4.1 x 5.8 inches and a maximum rated speed of 10,000 sets per hour. These are document-collator specifications, not demonstrated finished-card deck throughput; smaller finished cards require a different documented feeding solution. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dsc-10-60i-collator/
- [statement] Madison advertises card-line counting, stacking and banding for cards starting at 3 x 3 inches. Its SB-25 waits for a predetermined count or an upstream sort signal before banding; the advertised minimum size needs checking against the actual cards. (low confidence) — https://www.madisonbanders.com/applications/card-sorting-gift-cards

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Marden Edwards distinguishes LX, LX wide and LXH maximum wrapping rates as 70, 40 and 90 packs per minute, respectively, and explicitly says output depends on pack size. The 90-pack headline cannot be applied to every LX configuration or treated as measured complete-game output. (low confidence) — https://www.mardenedwards.com/machinery/overwrapping-machines/lx-series
- [statement] In a supplier-authored playing-card plant case study, EXAIR reports that cards stuck together and double-fed, and that static regenerated through the process. This is evidence of a real feeding failure mode; it does not establish a universal failure rate or quantified throughput improvement. (low confidence) — https://blog.exair.com/2022/01/19/playing-card-manufacturer-gets-dealt-a-bad-hand-from-static-electricity/
- [statement] TCG Machines documents feed-mechanism adjustment, dirty feed wheels, and insufficient card weight as causes of its PhyzBatch Refill Hopper error. This adjacent card-handling example shows why automated feeding still requires setup and maintenance; its intervals must not be transferred to a manufacturing line. (low confidence) — https://support.tcgmachines.com/knowledge/error-empty-hopper

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Rollem describes an Auto-Collator that combines sub-packs into complete sets and an additional in-line cello-wrap unit; this is evidence of a modular collation-to-wrapping workflow, rather than proof that a collator itself loads retail boxes. (low confidence) — https://www.rollemusa.com/feeding-delivery-units/ · keywords: Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://rollem.com/processes/collate/
- [statement] Pineberry lists standard CC-50 batch capabilities of 1–100. Its announcement for the 2018 ICMA exhibition additionally says higher counts are available. Treat the higher-count configuration as an unresolved specification. If a proposed stack exceeds the standard batch range, confirm the higher-count configuration rather than assuming the standard counter can process it in one batch. (low confidence) — https://www.pineberryinc.com/solutions/collectible-card-sorting-counting-machines/ · keywords: Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://www.pineberryinc.com/press-release/pineberry-manufacturing-to-demonstrate-the-cc-50-card-counter-at-icma-expo-2018/
- [statement] Uchida specifies EZC-250 items 0.2–0.8mm thick, 25–120mm wide and 40–150mm long, with a stack capacity up to 130mm. Items must be flat, uncurled and without burrs; nonrectangular shapes require testing. These are stock qualification limits rather than proof of compatibility with the game. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=287
- [statement] Uchida describes Countron OP as an optical counter using an optical sensor and air blow. Its standard TD1 sensor covers 0.18–0.35mm material and its specification says no tab tape insertion. Treat it as quantity-verification equipment, rather than an automatic physical separator for finished decks. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=285
- [statement] Rollem markets the AutoCollator for lower-volume and short-run card jobs, with collected decks presented to downstream wrapping or packing; these are described as downstream processes rather than functions established by the collator description. (low confidence) — https://rollem.com/processes/collate/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Collation, card counting, and banding are distinct operations: Rollem describes arranging cards into decks, Pineberry describes counting individual cards, and Madison describes counting, stacking and banding. Specify which operations a proposed line actually includes. (medium confidence) — https://rollem.com/processes/collate/ · keywords: Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://www.pineberryinc.com/solutions/collectible-card-sorting-counting-machines/, https://www.madisonbanders.com/applications/card-sorting-gift-cards
- [statement] The Morgana Countron AT Touch page specifies an optional small-paper attachment with a minimum size of seventy by one hundred sixty millimeters and tab insertion every 2–1,000 sheets. A sheet-counting specification must therefore be checked against the actual finished-card dimensions before selection. (low confidence) — https://plockmaticgroup.com/morgana/product/countron-touch-at/
- [statement] The same EXAIR case study describes a card-production line that boxed and labelled its output. It is an attributed example of downstream boxing automation. If a custom game is proposed, verify its required configuration before using the case-study line as a production model. (low confidence) — https://blog.exair.com/2022/01/19/playing-card-manufacturer-gets-dealt-a-bad-hand-from-static-electricity/
- [statement] Rollem describes SlipStream III collation as collecting rows of cards into sub-decks and sequencing them in a Pack Separation Unit; its software can combine multiple sub-decks so a deck may span multiple sheets or one sheet may produce multiple decks. This is manufacturer-described capability, not verification of the commissioned two-stack game. (low confidence) — https://rollem.com/news/monthly-new-feature-slipstream-iii-collator/
- [statement] Uchida specifies EZC-250 bottom-suction-belt counting at up to two hundred forty pieces per minute, variable; this rating measures counted items, not completed packed games. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/products/detail/id=287
- [statement] Uchida’s dated comparison warns that Countron Touch can curl the counted corner and recommends work where that portion can subsequently be removed. It says Countron AT Touch avoids curling. These are manufacturer statements, not independently demonstrated damage rates. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/news/detail/id=370
- [statement] In its August 02, 2024 comparison, Uchida specifies Countron AT Touch at 80–400gsm, thickness up to 0.4mm depending on stock, and a minimum sheet size of one hundred by one hundred forty-eight millimeters. A heavy-stock counting capability therefore does not establish compatibility with every finished card format. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/news/detail/id=370
- [statement] Uchida’s comparison describes programmable tab insertion at different sheet counts, including successive batches of 48, 24 and 60 sheets. This supports batch separation as a distinct operation; it does not establish card identity or sequence verification. (low confidence) — https://www.uchida-machinery.com/news/detail/id=370
- [statement] Duplo markets Esper DM-230V as a direct-mail collator with 23 feed stations and up to 9,000 sets per hour for leaflets, brochures and postcards; the integrated cover wraps a document set. Its described application and input envelope must not be treated as proof of finished small-card deck collation, film wrapping or cartoning. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/esper-dm-230v-direct-mail-collator/
- [statement] Jacob White lists semi-automatic and automatic cartoners for playing-card packaging, while stating that machine modifications have constraints based on the customer’s requirements. Listing a compatible machine family does not qualify the commissioned two-stack pack. (low confidence) — https://www.jacobwhite.com/packaging-types/playing-cards
- [statement] Jacob White’s NS-X 3.1 erects cartons automatically on operator demand but leaves product insertion to the operator; after loading, the machine applies glue, closes the flaps and discharges the carton. This is an example of automated carton handling with manual product loading. (low confidence) — https://www.jacobwhite.com/machine/ns-x-31-semi-automatic-cartoner
- [statement] Jacob White explicitly makes NS-X 3.1 output dependent on the carton and product, and describes its variable speed range as subject to size and board quality. A finished-game throughput assumption requires the actual pack configuration. (low confidence) — https://www.jacobwhite.com/machine/ns-x-31-semi-automatic-cartoner · keywords: Deck collation counting and packing automation · also: https://www.jacobwhite.com/packaging-types/playing-cards
- [statement] Marden Edwards’ application gallery identifies overwrapped game cards and standard playing-card packs with tear tape. This establishes a manufacturer application example; the gallery provides no demonstrated speed or two-stack loading result for the commissioned game. (low confidence) — https://www.mardenedwards.com/gallery
- [statement] In a February 21, 2018 installation announcement, NAPCO/Vulcan says it installed a Rollem MK2 Slipstream and describes inline collation, stacking, boxing and wrapping. Its stated 2,200 decks per hour is an operator-company announcement without a disclosed card-count configuration or independent time study; do not transfer that figure to the commissioned game. (low confidence) — https://vulcaninformationpackaging.com/napco-vulcan-introduce-playing-card-manufacturing/
